newsitem.title: UK: Yamaichi to close London futures/options.
newsitem.headline: Yamaichi to close London futures/options.

text.p: Yamaichi International (Europe) said on Thursday it planned to close its futures and options section in London over the next month, affecting 15 staff on the floor of LIFFE and on the bank's sales desk.
The Japanese bank said it could not justify the large amounts of capital needed to remain competitive in this market.

"Yamaichi has seats on the floor of LIFFE and a small sales and trading desk in its office on Finsbury Pavement and plans to wind down its F&O (futures and options) business over the next month," the bank said in a statement.

"Over the last two years, Yamaichi has successfully expanded its F&O operations. However, although the section is profitable, the company feels that to become a major player in this market would require large amounts of capital which could be utilised more effectively in other parts of its business," the bank said.
The announcement follows closely on news of a downgrade by rating agency Standard & Poor's on June 5.

S&P downgraded Yamaichi Securuties' long-term counterparty rating to BBB from BBB plus, citing the bank's prolonged poor performance and an expected negative impact from ongoing deregulation in the Japanese securities industry.
But the agency also revised the outlook to stable from negative and said this was because of restructuring efforts already in progress.

Santi Kalf, head of bond trading at Yamaichi, said in the statement: "With falling margins, it is our view that we cannot justify the major investment of capital needed to remain competitive in this market in the future."
